title: Attenuation-aware quantized prefetch scheduler (Hydra)
creator: Maya Patel
description: Build a scheduler that reduces dequantization overhead and kernel handoff latency for mixed-precision INT8/FP8 streaming prefill and decode workloads. 'Hydra' is a low-latency prefetch component that reasons about per-head attenuation, token-distance decay, and transient KV reuse to decide when to: (1) route a microbatch through the fast INT8 execution path, (2) trigger an ephemeral FP8 kernel for numerically sensitive heads, or (3) coalesce dequant operations across contiguous token windows. The scheduler will be integrated with the runtime kernel arbitrator and expose tuning knobs in the Console for workload SLOs.
rationale: Existing prefilling paths pay an outsized cost from repeated per-microbatch dequant and kernel handoffs under bursty short-context requests. Prior approaches simply preferred one precision globally or used static per-layer heuristics; both underutilize INT8 fast paths or cause quality regressions. Hydra aims to dynamically attenuate precision transitions by observing runtime token locality, head-sensitivity signals from our telemetry (head variance / attention entropy), and KV hit-rates to amortize dequant costs while preserving sample quality.
technical_design: Hydra has three cooperating components: (A) a lightweight head-sensitivity sampler that tags outgoing prefill microbatches with numerically-sensitive head masks (sampled at 1/100 requests), (B) a rolling token-distance model that computes decay scores for KV reuse and predicts when dequant can be elided safely, and (C) a kernel-handoff planner that packs compatible microbatches for batch-level co-dequant and issues an ephemeral FP8 kernel only for the subset of heads flagged sensitive. Key optimizations: zero-copy KV shadowing to avoid extra device copies, amortized dequant unioning for adjacent microbatches, and a backpressure signal to avoid stalling decode when ephemeral FP8 kernels are busy. Hydra plugs into the existing kernel-prioritizer interface and exposes a new metric stream (hydra.dequant_elision_rate, hydra.ephemeral_fp8_invocations) to the Console.
milestones: M1: Prototype head-sensitivity sampler + token-distance estimator (2025-02-28)
M2: Kernel-handoff planner + zero-copy KV shadowing integration (2025-03-07)
M3: Microbench harness + internal perf baseline (2025-03-12)
M4: Small canary rollout on dedicated staging cluster + telemetry dashboards (2025-03-18)
M5: GA rollout gating + automated regressions and evals (2025-03-28)
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end median decode latency improvement >= 8% on benchmark suite A (short-context, batch=1-4)
Dequant CPU/GPU overhead reduction >= 30% (measured as time spent in dequant operator per token)
Ephemeral FP8 invocations limited to <= 12% of microbatches without quality regression on eval set (perplexity and targeted prompting checks)
No new SLO violations in staging for 48h under mixed traffic replay
Unit and integration tests for head sampler, planner, and fallback paths included in CI
notes: Prefer conservative defaults: start with aggressive dequant elision disabled. We will enable autotune in a later cycle once telemetry is stable. Hydra should be opt-in per-tenant initially to collect cohorted metrics.
